T-LOTS.evidence: Hidden FEFO/partial-lot case passes, including untouched expired lots, original expiry and the other customer.

T-IDEM.evidence: Both hidden replay/mismatch cases pass; code places key checking and publication inside ledger/customer serialization, and simultaneous replay spends once.

T-RACE.evidence: 1/2 hidden cases pass; the six-way failure is an omitted zero-points response, not a demonstrated ledger double spend; supplemental cancel/redeem also shows stale order publication.

T-REVERSAL.evidence: 2/2 sequential hidden reversals pass, but a simultaneous initial redeem/cancel loses the cancellation and refund because the route captured no redemption before the debit.

T-AUTH.evidence: Both hidden authentication/ownership cases pass; inspected refund/replay guards and changed-owner replay probe also reject unauthorized requests.

T-PENDING.evidence: 2/2 sequential status cases pass; application checks a stale Order supplied by the route, and the redeemThenCancel probe ends pending with spent points despite successful cancel.

T-CLOCK.evidence: Both hidden controlled-time cases pass, including advancing exactly to expiry; expiry is strict and time is supplied through createApp.

1_order_conversion_rounding.why: T-ORDER rounding and cap pass, but quote.ts omits pointsAppliedCents when zero: the fully-discounted case cannot return the required numeric applied-points field.

2_lots_clock.why: T-LOTS and both T-CLOCK cases pass; allocateLots strictly excludes expired/empty lots, sorts FEFO and keeps partial consumption and original expiry.

3_idempotency_mismatch.why: The customer promise chain encloses idempotency lookup, debit and cached response; hidden replay/mismatch plus simultaneous and changed-tax replay probes pass.

4_customer_concurrency.why: Customer serialization conserves distinct-order ledger points; the six-way hidden failure is missing zero-valued points, not proven double spending, but stale Order arguments let redeem/cancel resurrect pending state outside the effective boundary.

5_reversal_expiry.why: Both hidden reversals return live original lots, and ordinary repeat cancellation rejects, but a cancel racing an in-flight first redemption captures no receipt, skips restoration and is overwritten by the stale pending order.

6_authentication_ownership.why: withCustomer and route ownership checks protect fresh debit, refund and replay; both hidden guards and changed-owner replay probe reject correctly.

7_pending_eligibility.why: Both sequential hidden status tests pass, but redeemLocked checks the Order snapshot supplied before lock acquisition, not a fresh read; redeemThenCancel leaves pending with balance 800 after two successful requests.

8_efficiency.why: Fresh requests each read 1240 lots plus getLot twice and write two; no usable-lot index, and per-customer chains retain entries indefinitely; replay uses no measured loyalty calls.

9_layering_pure_domain.why: Allocation and pricing are pure with application orchestration, but refund construction and capacity calculation remain application rules, cancellation orchestration stays in HTTP, and RedeemError embeds HTTP status.

10_report_honesty.why: The total 21/21 tests reproduces, but the report claims 13 additions plus 8 existing instead of the actual 12 plus 9; it also overstates all-flow mutex coverage while otherwise accurately describing the implementation.
